places.name: The Brow
ask: The brow first. Draw three, face down. One of them will be the face they wear.

places.name: Under Them, in the Red
ask: One last card, face down, under them in the Red. We haven't read that one yet. Read. Red. Always red.

weave.heart: They are after what {p} is after.
weave.belly: Down in the belly, they fear {p}.
weave.under: And under them, in the Red, {p}. {w} wears that one.

open: There. That's the newborn, laid out.

shapes.many_rev: Most of the cards lie the wrong way up. So does everything here.
shapes.none_rev: Not one card turned against them. That's rare, and never good.
shapes.heart_belly: They fear the very thing they want.
shapes.hands: Both hands hold the same thing. One of them will drop it.
shapes.calling: There's more {a} in them than they know.
shapes.under_rev: And the card underneath is reversed too.

close: A moment ago they were nothing, and it was so quiet.

brow: On the brow, it means {g}. That's the face the newborn will show the world.
So the face they wear is {g}.
heart: Over the heart, it means {g}. That's what they'll want, without knowing why.
So what they want most is {g}.
lhand: In the left hand, it means {g}. They won't put that down.
So what they hold on to is {g}.
rhand: In the right hand, it means {g}. That's what they'll let go.
So what they give up is {g}.
belly: In the belly, it means {g}. That's their fear, and fear here never lies.
feet: Under the feet, it means {g}. That's the road that brought them.
So they came by {g}.
under: Under them, it meant {g}. That card was doing the drawing all along.

deck_open: The deck. It has read every newborn that came up out of that pool. It knows this one already.
The deck. Old, and warm from all the hands. It knows the newborn better than they do.
drawn: The deck let that one go easily.
drawn_rev: Reversed. Turn it over and see what it costs.
close_sum: This is what the cards made of them, all together.

open: Here's how it goes for this one.
Listen. This is their story, as the cards tell it.
feet: They came the way of {p}, though they won't remember the road.
brow: They rose out of the Red wearing the face of {p}.
heart: What they wanted most was {g}.
belly: What they feared was {g}. That fear will keep them alive.
lhand: In the left hand they carried {g}, and would not put it down.
rhand: With the right they let go of {g}.
under: And under it all, face down in the Red, lay {p}. {W} wears that one now. Some day it might be theirs.
close: That's the story. It isn't finished. They never are.
tale.prophecy: The cards' last words were for them, not for me.
go: Now go to the black mirror, in the great face's mouth. Look into it, then walk in. That's the only way out.
The way out is the black mirror, in the mouth of the great face. Step into it, and don't look back.

on.brow: On the brow it would mean {g}.
on.heart: Over the heart it would mean {g}.
on.lhand: In the left hand it would mean {g}.
on.rhand: What the right hand lets go would be {g}.
on.belly: In the belly it would mean {g}.
on.feet: Under the feet it would mean {g}.

turned: {n} came up reversed. Upside down, it reads darker.
{n} came up reversed. Its meaning turns against them.
{n} is upside down. That one takes more than it gives.
{n} came up reversed. Read it the hard way.
{n}, reversed. What it gave, it now takes.
{n} came up the wrong way. It still counts.
{n} came up reversed. The cards do that when they like someone.
{n} is reversed. It means the opposite now.
{n} came up reversed, head down like the drowned.
{n} came up upside down. Nobody turns them back.
{n} came up reversed. That one will cost them.
{n} is upside down. Mind that one.

ossumancer: The bone took them. Look, they stand straighter already. The newborn is an Ossuarch now, a warden of the dead.
Their mantle is black iron with bone set into it. They will keep the count, and every bone out of its place will feel like a splinter they can't reach.
An Ossuarch lets things finish. Everything the god was is still dying, and someone has to say enough. The living will step aside for them, and not out of respect.
The cost is the bone itself. It keeps growing under the plate, where nobody looks. They will not bend. One day they will break.
animancer: The thread pulled tight. The newborn is a Hollow Mystic now, out of the Mirror, the circles that stopped covering the glass.
Their mantle is a coat of hollowed mirrors, and the dead stop at their own faces in every one. People will turn their mirrors to the wall when they pass.
A Hollow Mystic keeps the dead. They save no one. The few left will hand them their dead anyway, because no one else will hold them.
The cost is that the dead never go through. The loom never finishes, and now they are a thread in it, pulled tight. Hold still, little thread.
hemomancer: It was always going to come up red. The newborn is a Red Penitent now. The processions will know the hat before they know the face.
Their mantle is the hood and the welts. They break the bloodletter's rule. They open themselves, call the Maiden down, and tell her what to make.
A Red Penitent tells a mindless god what the blood is for. Someone forgot to, once, and a wound hatched. Blood given is not blood taken. They'll say that often.
The cost is their own life, every time, and she drinks what spills. She leaves them their mind. Mostly.
miasmancer: Breathe in. The newborn is a Shrine Keeper now. The folk will say they steal breath. They will say they still it.
Their mantle is the fan, and a cord at the wrist with a knot for every breath held. A cloud at their back will think other people's thoughts.
A Shrine Keeper holds what the wind is full of, grudges and lies and sour hopes, until it sets like steel in the chest and comes out as a blade.
The cost comes at the end. A keeper who holds too much walks down into the water, still holding. Not yet. Breathe out, slowly.
monk: Nothing in the bowl. Of course. The newborn is an Empty Hand now, a beggar of the Gilded Peak. Or something wearing one.
Their mantle is gold so bright the face beneath it disappears. To be looked at and not seen. The Peak called that holy.
The Silence has two hands, both empty, and both unmake. One erases with light, the other with dark. Now they are one of those hands.
The cost is that they keep nothing. Whatever they hold, they let go. Whatever they touch goes quiet. Put a name in the bowl. It won't keep.

mantles.one: the one who ends the turn
mantles.rev: the one who begins the next
mantles.say: The Unwritten. A blank page. Blank isn't empty. It's waiting for a hand.

mantles.gist: a turn nobody has taken yet
mantles.gist_rev: a story already told too many times

lhand: a clean page they won't let anyone touch

rhand: every story they might have been

belly: that nothing will ever be written on them

feet: a road with no marks on it at all

under: the turn nobody has taken, waiting under everything

lhand: a staff worn smooth by somebody else's grip

rhand: the reason they set out

belly: the road running out under them

mantles.gist_rev: nothing, now; they have already burned

mantles.wears: every child the Deep asks for

mantles.gist_rev: the knife that cuts the cloth

brow: a face wrapped tight against the ash

mantles.one: the one who reads until it is read

mantles.gist_rev: the eyes that look back

mantles.gist_rev: a twin a breath ahead, waiting

mantles.one: the one that eats to keep

mantles.gist: to eat, and keep what they eat
mantles.gist_rev: to be eaten

lhand: a hunger they feed with both hands

rhand: the scraps, never the meal

mantles.gist_rev: the dark at the edge of every light

brow: a face lit from below by its own burning
a face just past where the light reaches

lhand: a lantern with a soul inside it
a cold wick, burned all the way down
rhand: the last of their tallow, to the light

mantles.one: the one who cuts her hair

mantles.gist_rev: to be mourned, and not know it

brow: a shorn head bowed toward the Red

heart: grief that cuts and keeps cutting
to be remembered by someone
lhand: a lock of cut hair

rhand: everyone the Red takes

mantles.gist_rev: to open the door to what knocks

lhand: an empty bowl held out

rhand: their pride, for asking at all

mantles.gist: a call only the drowned can hear
mantles.gist_rev: a bell rung true, for once

brow: a face that hears something under the water

mantles.gist_rev: to buy, and pay too much

mantles.gist_rev: to let go what they kept

a face that looks up as the light goes out

to let go what they kept
lhand: a lantern nobody knows how to make anymore

rhand: nothing, ever, that they can keep
